messages:

Subject: Private deployment: licensing structure, support band & environment count — follow-up

Hi Tom — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and the asks we called out so we can put a preliminary proposal together: 

1) Volume & unit economics (you mentioned steady-state and pilot):
- Pilot: ~50M tokens / month (inference) for a 3-month pilot.
- Target steady-state: 8–12B tokens / month in year 1 (traffic grows after model rollout).
- Target unit cost: you mentioned wanting ~ $700–900 / 1M tokens equivalent (goal: compare hosted vs private unit economics).

2) Licensing model preference:
- Two logical models we discussed: capacity-based reserved slots (monthly commitment) vs. per-token + platform fee. We typically propose a hybrid: base reservation for guaranteed throughput + overage per-million-tokens.

3) Environments / isolation:
- You indicated two VPCs: Prod and Staging, plus a shared sandbox for data-science experiments — so 3 environments. Confirm if each needs separate HW pools and dedicated KV-cache persistence.

4) Support tier & compliance:
- Standard (business hours) vs. Premium (24/7 + faster response + quarterly architectural reviews). Please confirm desired tier — this drives uplift on licensing and SLA.

Next steps (what we will do):
- I attached a short licensing slide and an env-count workbook to capture expected instance types and throughput per environment.
- Marissa (pricing lead) will sketch two commercial options: (A) Reserved + overage (monthly commit), (B) Platform license + per-token.
- Karthik will run a sizing pass assuming 8B tokens/month and return estimated GPU pool counts & monthly cost curve.

Could you: confirm the 3 envs + whether sandbox requires full isolation, confirm target $/1M tokens range, and include your procurement contact (copied here is Sally?) if different.

Thanks — aiming to get a draft commercial by Wednesday EOD.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_Private_Licensing_v1.pdf (slides), env_count_workbook.xlsx (workbook)

Subject: Re: Private deployment: licensing structure, support band & environment count — follow-up

Thanks Mina — great recap. Quick answers: 

- Pilot numbers are correct (~50M tokens/mo). Steady-state estimate is closer to 10B tokens/mo after Q2 next year.
- For unit economics target — the execs want to see options that hit <= $800 / 1M tokens on steady-state. If we can get to ~$700 that's a win.
- Environments: yes, Prod + Staging + Sandbox. Sandbox does not require full HW isolation; we can accept shared worker pools but would like logical isolation and separate artifact stores.
- Support: leaning toward Premium for the first 12 months given regulatory posture.

Procurement: Sally (copied) is our procurement lead — she will coordinate contract review and has asked to see an initial SOW and indicative TCO.

Questions from our side: 1) How big an uplift is Premium support (ballpark % uplift on license)? 2) If we start with 3 environments but later add a fourth (training/ftw), how do you price incremental environments?

Happy to sync again briefly tomorrow if helpful.

Thanks Tom — helpful. Quick replies inline below and a couple clarifications.

1) Premium support uplift: typically +18–25% on top of the platform/license line depending on response-time SLAs and included blocks of architecture time. Marissa will provide a range.

2) Incremental environments: we price primary environments (Prod + Staging) at full environment fee; additional logical environments that can share worker pools (like your Sandbox) are priced at a reduced environment add-on (typically 25–40% of full environment fee). If a later training environment requires dedicated pools, it would be priced as a full environment. We will map the expected resource utilization in the env_count_workbook to give precise deltas.

3) Unit cost: to hit ~$700–800 / 1M tokens steady-state we generally recommend a mix of quantized model variants (4-bit where acceptable) + aggressive KV caching for repeated prompts + reserved throughput buckets. Karthik will model GPU types for that profile.

Next: Marissa — can you draft two commercial sketches (hybrid reserved + overage; and platform license + per-token) aimed at the 10B tokens/mo target and show the landed $/1M token for each?

Sally — we'll prepare an initial SOW and TCO doc. We plan to have a draft in your hands by Wednesday EOD (Nov 1 — sorry, typo, we mean Dec 2). If that timeline doesn't work for procurement, flag here.

Best,
Mina

Subject: Pricing sketches for MedTech AI — two options (indicative)

Tom / Mina / Sally — looping in the pricing sketches as asked. High-level notes up front: these are indicative commercial sketches to validate whether we are in the right ballpark. Final pricing depends on confirmed env sizing and model profile.

Option A — Hybrid Reserved + Overage (preferred for predictability):
- Commitment: reserved capacity equivalent to baseline 6B tokens/mo (monthly commit).
- Overage: billed per 1M tokens for usage above commit.
- Platform fee (monthly): $40k
- Reserved uplift (monthly): $70k (covers baseline throughput + reserved GPU pools)
- Premium support uplift: +20% on license lines (platform + reserved).
- Indicative landed unit cost at 10B tokens/mo: ~$760 / 1M tokens (assumes 6B reserved, 4B metered).

Option B — Platform license + Per-token (simple for procurement):
- Platform fee (monthly): $55k
- Per-token metered rate: $1,050 / 1M tokens for first 5B, volume tiers apply beyond.
- Premium support uplift: +20% on platform fee only.
- Indicative landed unit cost at 10B tokens/mo (with standard discounts applied): ~$810 / 1M tokens.

Environments & add-ons:
- Prod: full environment fee included in reserved pool.
- Staging: full environment fee included.
- Sandbox: logical environment add-on at 30% of full env fee (shared worker pools).
- Additional dedicated training env: priced as a full additional environment.

Attachments: I exported a short TCO table into the env_count_workbook.xlsx (see attached). Next step: if these ranges look reasonable, we can convert Option A into a redlined SOW + a three-month pilot amendment.

Can you confirm whether Option A or B is directionally preferred? Also confirm the sandbox can be shared (we have it as shared in the workbook).

Thanks — Marissa
Pricing Lead, Redwood Inference
